AD_ELEMENT.NAME: Processed At
AD_ELEMENT.HELP: When delivery finished with this event, in UTC. Every timestamp the module writes is UTC rather than the session time zone, so comparing one against another is meaningful wherever the server and the client happen to be.
AD_ELEMENT.DESCRIPTION: Moment the event reached a terminal state

AD_ELEMENT.NAME: Vector Dimensions
AD_ELEMENT.DESCRIPTION: Length of the embedding vector
AD_ELEMENT.HELP: Must match what the model returns. Limited to 2000, which is the ceiling for an indexable vector column.

AD_ELEMENT.NAME: Embedding Model
AD_ELEMENT.DESCRIPTION: Provider model identifier, for example text-embedding-3-small
AD_ELEMENT.HELP: Model that produces the embeddings, as the endpoint names it, for instance text-embedding-3-small. A provider-agnostic gateway such as the Etendo LLM proxy serves more than one provider and has to be told which one to use: there the format is "provider/model", for instance openai/text-embedding-3-small. Changing this on a source that already has a collection does not re-embed anything, and if the new model has a different vector size the collection no longer matches -- activation reports that rather than repairing it, because repairing means dropping every vector it holds.

AD_ELEMENT.NAME: Embedding Content
AD_ELEMENT.DESCRIPTION: When checked, the value of this column is part of the embedded text
AD_ELEMENT.HELP: Unchecked columns are still stored as filterable metadata, they just do not contribute to the vector.

AD_ELEMENT.NAME: Vector Source Column
AD_ELEMENT.DESCRIPTION: Column of the source table contributing to the embedding

AD_ELEMENT.NAME: Search Target Key
AD_ELEMENT.HELP: The name a caller uses to search this target through the API. It is part of the contract with whoever integrates: changing it breaks every caller already asking for the old one.
AD_ELEMENT.DESCRIPTION: Stable identifier API clients use to select this search target

AD_ELEMENT.NAME: Embedding Provider
AD_ELEMENT.DESCRIPTION: Provider used to turn the source content into vectors
AD_ELEMENT.HELP: Defines the model and its dimensions. Changing it on a populated source makes the existing vectors incomparable with the new ones.

AD_ELEMENT.NAME: Estimated Records
AD_ELEMENT.DESCRIPTION: Approximate number of records the source table holds
AD_ELEMENT.HELP: Taken from the table statistics once, when the reindex starts. It is an estimate meant to show progress, not an exact count: counting exactly would scan the whole table on every refresh.

AD_ELEMENT.NAME: Vector Reindex Request
AD_ELEMENT.DESCRIPTION: A pending full reindex of a source

AD_ELEMENT.NAME: Distance Metric
AD_ELEMENT.DESCRIPTION: How similarity between embeddings is measured
AD_ELEMENT.HELP: Cosine is the recommended default for text embeddings. It is applied when the vector collection is created.

AD_ELEMENT.NAME: API Key Reference
AD_ELEMENT.DESCRIPTION: Name of the property, environment variable or Openbravo.properties entry holding the key
AD_ELEMENT.HELP: This is the name of where the key lives, never the key itself. The value is stored in clear text and exported with the module dataset.

AD_ELEMENT.NAME: Retry Limit
AD_ELEMENT.HELP: How many times a failed event is handed back to delivery before it is left alone. It stops a permanent failure -- a model that no longer exists, a revoked key -- from being retried forever at the provider's expense. An event that reached the limit stays failed and visible in the Outbox Monitor, where it can be sent back to the queue once the cause is fixed.
AD_ELEMENT.DESCRIPTION: Delivery attempts before an event stops being recovered automatically

AD_ELEMENT.NAME: Filter Display Logic
AD_ELEMENT.DESCRIPTION: Expression restricting which indexed records this target returns
AD_ELEMENT.HELP: Uses display logic syntax over the configured metadata columns, for example @IsSOTrx@='Y'. Field names must be columns configured on the source.

AD_ELEMENT.NAME: API Endpoint
AD_ELEMENT.DESCRIPTION: Base URL of the embeddings API. Leave empty to use the provider default
AD_ELEMENT.HELP: Optional. Base URL of an OpenAI-compatible embeddings API, up to and including /v1 and no further: the path of the call is added by the module and is never configured here. Leave it empty to call OpenAI itself. Point it at the Etendo LLM proxy (https://llm.etendo.software/v1), an Azure OpenAI deployment, a corporate gateway or a local stub to use the same configuration against any of them. When the endpoint is a provider-agnostic gateway, name the provider in the Embedding Model field as well.

AD_ELEMENT.NAME: Request Timeout
AD_ELEMENT.HELP: How long a single embedding request may take before it is abandoned. It bounds one request, not the whole delivery run: the event it belonged to is marked as failed and retried later, up to the retry limit. Too low a value turns a slow provider into a stream of failures; too high a one holds a delivery thread while the queue grows.
AD_ELEMENT.DESCRIPTION: Seconds to wait for an embedding response before failing the event

AD_ELEMENT.NAME: Embedding Batch Size
AD_ELEMENT.DESCRIPTION: Number of texts sent per provider request
AD_ELEMENT.HELP: Bounds both the provider request and the transaction the scheduled process holds while delivering it.

AD_ELEMENT.NAME: Vector Search Target
AD_ELEMENT.DESCRIPTION: A named, filterable entry point for vector search

AD_ELEMENT.NAME: Event Type
AD_ELEMENT.HELP: What happened to the record that produced this event: INSERT and UPDATE re-embed it, DELETE removes its vector. It is written by the database trigger, never by hand.
AD_ELEMENT.DESCRIPTION: Operation that produced the event

AD_ELEMENT.NAME: Index On Delete
AD_ELEMENT.HELP: Whether deleting a record removes its vector. Turning it off leaves the vectors of deleted records in the collection, where a search will keep returning them.
AD_ELEMENT.DESCRIPTION: Remove the embedding when a record is deleted

AD_ELEMENT.NAME: Last Error
AD_ELEMENT.HELP: What the provider or the database answered the last time this failed. It is the first thing to read when events pile up: a revoked key, a model that no longer exists and a source with no content column all stop delivery, and only this says which.
AD_ELEMENT.DESCRIPTION: Message of the most recent failed attempt

AD_ELEMENT.NAME: Vector Search Source
AD_ELEMENT.DESCRIPTION: The vector search source this record belongs to
AD_ELEMENT.HELP: Identifies which table is indexed, under which namespace, and with which embedding provider.

AD_ELEMENT.NAME: Enqueued Records
AD_ELEMENT.HELP: How many records the backfill has enqueued so far. It counts events written to the outbox, not vectors stored: delivery happens afterwards, so this reaching the total only means the queue is complete, not that the index is.
AD_ELEMENT.DESCRIPTION: How many records this reindex has enqueued so far

AD_ELEMENT.NAME: Index On Update
AD_ELEMENT.HELP: Whether changing a watched column enqueues an event. The trigger only fires for the columns marked Reindex On Change and only when the value really changed, so a save that touches nothing else costs nothing.
AD_ELEMENT.DESCRIPTION: Enqueue an indexing event when a watched column changes

AD_ELEMENT.NAME: Index On Insert
AD_ELEMENT.HELP: Whether a new record enqueues an event. Turning it off leaves records created from now on out of the index until a backfill picks them up.
AD_ELEMENT.DESCRIPTION: Enqueue an indexing event when a record is created

AD_ELEMENT.NAME: Indexing Enabled
AD_ELEMENT.DESCRIPTION: When checked, changes to the source table are captured for indexing
AD_ELEMENT.HELP: Disabling it removes the generated database triggers on the next update.database.

AD_ELEMENT.NAME: Activate Vector Indexing
AD_ELEMENT.DESCRIPTION: Reports whether the selected sources are ready to be indexed by the next update.database
AD_ELEMENT.HELP: Reports whether the selected sources are ready to be indexed, and what is stopping the ones that are not. It changes nothing in the database. Everything a source needs -- the pgvector extension, the runtime storage, its collection and its change capture triggers -- is created by the next update.database, because creating them while the application runs makes that update refuse to start. So the order is: configure the source, press this to check it, then run update.database. Selecting every row is a sensible way to use it, and running it again is always harmless.

AD_ELEMENT.NAME: Reindex On Change
AD_ELEMENT.HELP: Whether a change to this column enqueues a re-embedding. Leave it off for a column that is only metadata to filter by, so editing it does not pay for an embedding that would come out the same.
AD_ELEMENT.DESCRIPTION: A change in this column enqueues a re-embedding of the record

AD_ELEMENT.NAME: Vector Outbox Event
AD_ELEMENT.DESCRIPTION: A queued indexing event

AD_ELEMENT.NAME: Attempt Count
AD_ELEMENT.DESCRIPTION: Delivery attempts so far
AD_ELEMENT.HELP: Compared against the retry limit of the source provider to decide whether an abandoned event is recovered or retired.

AD_ELEMENT.NAME: Configuration Version
AD_ELEMENT.DESCRIPTION: Version counter of the source configuration
AD_ELEMENT.HELP: Every queued event carries the version it was created under. Events from an older version are discarded instead of indexed.

AD_ELEMENT.NAME: Status
AD_ELEMENT.HELP: Where the event is in delivery. PENDING is waiting, PROCESSING has been claimed by a run, DONE was embedded and stored, FAILED gave up after the provider retry limit, and SUPERSEDED was discarded because the source configuration changed after the event was enqueued and re-embedding it would have stored a vector nobody asked for. Only the scheduled process writes this: a claim is an update guarded by the previous status, so editing it by hand can hand one event to two runs at once.
AD_ELEMENT.DESCRIPTION: Lifecycle state of the record

AD_ELEMENT.NAME: Last Enqueued Record
AD_ELEMENT.DESCRIPTION: Key of the last record enqueued by this reindex
AD_ELEMENT.HELP: The reindex walks the source table in key order and stores how far it got, so an interrupted run continues from there instead of starting over. Written by the process.

AD_ELEMENT.NAME: Provider Type
AD_ELEMENT.HELP: Which API dialect the endpoint speaks. OpenAI is the only one implemented, and it is also what every OpenAI-compatible gateway serves, so it is the right choice for the Etendo LLM proxy and for an Azure OpenAI deployment as well. It is not the name of the company behind the model: that goes in the Embedding Model field when the endpoint serves several.
AD_ELEMENT.DESCRIPTION: Embedding backend implementation

AD_ELEMENT.NAME: Vector Namespace
AD_ELEMENT.DESCRIPTION: Logical partition under which the embeddings of this source are stored
AD_ELEMENT.HELP: Must match an existing vector collection. A value with no collection fails at search time with VECTOR_COLLECTION_NOT_FOUND.

AD_ELEMENT.NAME: Max Input Characters
AD_ELEMENT.HELP: Longest text sent for a single record; anything beyond this is cut off before the request leaves. It exists because a model rejects an input past its token limit and the whole batch fails with it, so one oversized record would stop the records batched alongside it. Characters are not tokens: leave room, as a token is roughly four characters for English text and fewer for other languages.
AD_ELEMENT.DESCRIPTION: Content longer than this is truncated before embedding

AD_ELEMENT.NAME: Filter Column
AD_ELEMENT.HELP: Optional. Indexes only the records whose column matches Filter Value, instead of the whole table. The filter is compiled into the database trigger, so a record that does not match never reaches the queue at all -- which is also why changing it does not remove the vectors of records that matched before.
AD_ELEMENT.DESCRIPTION: Column of the source table compared against the filter value

AD_ELEMENT.NAME: Filter Value
AD_ELEMENT.DESCRIPTION: Value the filter column is compared against
AD_ELEMENT.HELP: Together with the filter column it restricts which records are enqueued. The comparison is compiled into the generated trigger, so changes take effect after the next update.database.

AD_ELEMENT.NAME: Request Reindex
AD_ELEMENT.DESCRIPTION: Asks for the records the source already held to be indexed
AD_ELEMENT.HELP: The triggers only capture what changes from the moment they are installed, so a source configured over a table that already has rows indexes nothing until those rows are walked. Select the sources and press this button to ask for that walk; the scheduled process does it, in bounded chunks, so a table of millions of rows neither holds your session nor fills the queue faster than delivery drains it. The message tells you roughly how many records you just asked for. A source has one request for its whole life, so asking again starts it over and the counters of the previous walk are lost. A walk already in progress is left alone, and a source that could not be delivered is refused rather than queued.
